misconceptions.description: Judging an AI suggestion by how confident and well-written it sounds rather than against a learning theory or standard
misconceptions.trigger: teacher accepts a suggestion because it reads professionally, without checking it against the objective
misconceptions.feedback: Hold each suggestion against the lesson objective and an instructional principle. Fluent phrasing is not pedagogical justification.

misconceptions.description: Letting an attractive AI activity replace the lesson objective instead of serving it
misconceptions.trigger: teacher keeps a fun AI-suggested activity that does not assess or build the stated objective
misconceptions.feedback: Trace the activity back to the objective. If it does not move students toward the target, it is decoration, however engaging.

misconceptions.description: Assuming an AI suggestion that suits the median student also serves the range of learners in the room
misconceptions.trigger: teacher adopts a suggestion without checking it against the class's reading levels, accommodations, or language needs
misconceptions.feedback: Compare the suggestion against your actual learner variability, not a generic class. A good median move can still fail the margins.

misconceptions.description: Quietly downgrading the objective verb (explain becomes match, analyze becomes identify) so an appealing AI-suggested activity fits the lesson.
misconceptions.trigger: teacher rewrites or reinterprets the objective at a lower cognitive level so the engaging activity can stay unchanged
misconceptions.feedback: Hold the verb fixed and raise the activity to it; never lower the goal to fit the activity. If the activity only produces matching, add the component that forces explaining (a sentence-stem justification, a compare-and-defend step) or replace the activity.
